Resolves #20376

🌿 A Workstation spec no longer needs a Brain checkout just because its app runs a SharedWorker.

The off-socket `neuralLink` fixture now reaches a page's own SharedWorker App Worker. Ada's `attachPageSharedAppWorker` binds it through the browser's CDP targets, matched by `browserContextId`, under the same writer-pair, refusal and lifetime contracts as the dedicated path; a dedicated App Worker always wins. 21 single-page specs on SharedWorker apps join `ADAPTER_ELIGIBLE_SPECS`, and the engine tier names them in `RUN_PATHS`, so none loses hosted coverage on leaving the Brain tier. The GPU population now counts only the workstation specs `RUN_PATHS` does not name, and `SparseUpdatesNL` leaves `BRAIN_SMOKE`. Grace chose this shape for her #20328 surface (option 1 of my Tier-2.5 fork).

Evidence: L3 (local off-socket and Bridge runs, unit suites, before/after selection counts on one tree) → L3 required (AC-1 to AC-5). Residual: three specs stay Brain-gated with stated reasons (below). Residual-Owner: #20451.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationOffSocketContractNL.spec.mjs`, "the fixture pair writes through the page's SharedWorker…", now in `RUN_PATHS`; unit `sharedWorkerAppWorker.spec.mjs`, "serves the page's SharedWorker under the fixture's pair, releasing that pair before the session closes". |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same e2e test refuses an `{agentId}`-only call with "full {agentId, sessionId} writer pair", and the write never lands. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: "two pages sharing the SharedWorker keep their pairs' writes and lifetimes apart" (one `targetId`, a conflict on the other pair's subtree, and releasing B leaves A's locks); unit "two pages sharing one SharedWorker each dispatch and release only their own pair". |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: unit "a page with a dedicated App Worker never opens a browser CDP session"; the 44 dedicated entries are unchanged in the set. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `externalBrainSelection.spec.mjs` and `E2eCiSelection.spec.mjs` pin the predicate and the floor. Before → after on one tree (207 spec files): Brain-gated 91 → 70; Brain-free 116 → 137; engine tier executes 110 → 131; GPU-excluded 5 → 5; eligible set 44 → 65. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The engine tier's `RUN_PATHS` and GPU count changed too.** The ticket named only the eligibility predicate, but `test/playwright/e2e/workstation` sat outside `RUN_PATHS` as the GPU population. Eligible Workstation specs would have left the Brain tier without entering any hosted run, even though they run green hosted in the Brain tier today.
- **Three candidates stay Brain-gated:**
  - `workstation/DockSplitterZoneIdNL`, "3 consecutive boots", fails off-socket 3/3 and passes over the Bridge 2/2. The SharedWorker handle does not survive the test's re-boots.
  - `workstation/WorkstationNestedColumnResizeNL` flaked once in 4 off-socket runs, in its reverse-cancel arm.
  - `workstation/WorkstationMaximizeTabOverflowNL` has an open hosted-flake note from 11-06.

  The required tier does not inherit a known red.
- Ada authored the fixture and contract commits (`64bd568fe6`, `ddc2abffc3`); this PR merges `dev` and adds the selection.

## Test Evidence

Run locally on this branch: Chromium, `playwright.config.e2e.mjs`, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` unset (off-socket), remote token unset.
- **24 candidates off-socket:** 72 passed, 2 failed (22 of 24 files green, including the contract spec 2/2).
- **Discrimination:**
  - Off-socket `--repeat-each=3`: `DockSplitterZoneIdNL:66` failed 3/3 with the dock host never visible; `WorkstationNestedColumnResizeNL` passed 9/9.
  - Bridge control on an isolated port: both files green (5/5).
- **Units:** `externalBrainSelection`, `E2eCiSelection`, `sharedWorkerAppWorker` and `dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink` specs, 52 passed. After the `dev` merge with #20411, the seven selection-related unit specs pass 173.
- **CI unit leak, fixed in `8b578481ea`:** `sharedWorkerAppWorker.spec.mjs`'s fake workers swapped `globalThis.Neo` around an `await`. Overlapping evaluations restored each other's fake and left one behind, so the next spec in the worker failed (`toolbar/KeyboardNavigation.spec.mjs:87`, `Neo.ns is not a function`). Each evaluation now runs in its own `vm` context, and an `afterAll` pins the realm's `Neo`. The pair run that spec + `KeyboardNavigation` with `--repeat-each=3` passes 33/33. A separate leak in `dev`'s own `dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.spec.mjs` (it leaves `useDomIds` falsy for an adjacent toolbar spec, and `dev`'s copy reproduces it) is out of scope, noted in defect-note `c99f339a`.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted in Engine. The baseline jobs run in CI.

## Addressed Review Feedback

Responding to review https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/20461#pullrequestreview-5802935359:

**Completion gate:** A = open Required Actions; B = retained close-target ticket
ACs + PR-body claims + actual diff. A is empty relative to B at this head.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Bind the SharedWorker handle to the page's actual App Worker, or refuse ambiguous same-context App-worker candidates instead of choosing the first one. Add a discriminator with two matching targets in one context plus the existing cross-context positive control; a page for root B must never dispatch into root A.
      **Commit:** `e9b8717700`
      **Details:** Both halves. The helper reads, in the page's own main thread, the exact script URL its worker Manager loads the App Worker from: `(workers.app.basePath || workerBasePath) + fileName`, resolved against `document.baseURI`, the way `Manager#createWorker` builds it. It then matches context plus that URL. Two candidates for the URL throw `AmbiguousSharedAppWorkerError`, which the fixture reports at once instead of as an init timeout. Until the page names its script, the helper returns null and opens no session. The new unit arm puts root A and root B in one context, binds a root-B page to root B, and records root A as never attached; the cross-context arm is unchanged. Further arms cover the ambiguous pair and the no-URL-yet case. All three go red against the previous helper.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Detach the newly created browser CDP session when attachment/setup fails before the handle is returned, including a target disappearing between listing and attachment. Add a focused failure-path control proving the session is released while the original error remains observable.
      **Commit:** `e9b8717700`
      **Details:** Everything between `newBrowserCDPSession()` and the returned handle sits in one `try`, whose `catch` detaches and rethrows the original error. The new arm makes `Target.attachToTarget` throw "No target with given id found": the call rejects with that message, and the session is detached. It goes red against the previous helper.

**Evidence at `e9b8717700`, local:**
- **Units:** both adapter specs pass 19/19. A control with the previous helper restored fails exactly the 4 new arms.
- **Real browser, off-socket:** the page-derived URL equals the CDP target URL on the Workstation, dashboard and portal apps. One consequence surfaced: the contract spec's second page attached right after `goto`, before its Neo main thread named its script. It now waits for `Manager.workers.app`, and the spec passes 6/6 across 3 repeats.
- **Regression:** all 21 admitted specs pass off-socket again (68 tests, none failed or flaky).

CI status: pending on current head `e9b8717700`. The re-review request follows once CI is green.
